# LanguageSwitch The language switch of every Efolusi site: one short code per language (ID, EN), each a link to the same page in that language. Put it in the `actions` of `SiteHeader` beside `ThemeToggle`, or in the language slot of `SiteFooter`. It lives in the marketing group with the header and footer that hold it. Use it where a page can be read in more than one language. Give every language its own `href` (the product knows the other URL; Meridian fetches and stores nothing). Each link carries `hreflang` and `lang` with the language's code, and an accessible name that spells the language in itself and ends with the visible code: `Bahasa Indonesia (ID)`, `English (EN)`, so a voice user can say "click ID". The language in use is marked `aria-current="true"` and is not a link: a link to the page you are on does nothing. Pass `name` for any code other than `en` and `id`. Each target is 44px at a coarse pointer. At a fine pointer `size="md"` (default) is 36px (30px in compact density), as the `ThemeToggle` and the header menu button, and `size="sm"` is 28px (24px in compact density), never less than 24px. The focus ring comes from the library, and the only motion is the colour transition. ```jsx ``` It renders plain `` elements, as `SiteHeader` and `SiteFooter` do: a language change loads the page in the other language, so a full navigation is right. With Next.js, build each `href` from the locale route; `next/link` is not needed. `SiteHeader` renders `actions` twice (the bar and the mobile panel), so the switch uses no `id`. On a site without React, copy the markup: `
  • ID
  • EN
`.
